about.title: Citrus Heights Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You are on the floor of a grocery aisle off Greenback Lane, or on a cracked walkway outside an apartment complex near Auburn Boulevard, and the only thought is getting back up. In Citrus Heights, as across California, whether the property owner answers for your injuries comes down to notice: did they know about the spill, the loose mat or the missing handrail, or should they have found it with reasonable care, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? That question is settled with evidence that fades fast. Cleaning logs get overwritten, store cameras record over themselves within days, and a broken stair gets patched before anyone photographs it. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We link Citrus Heights residents with an independent attorney who can act on that evidence early, explain how pure comparative fault may shape your claim, and take the case on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Citrus Heights Residents Use LawProactive

items.title: Attorneys who focus on the notice question
items.desc: California premises cases turn on proving the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network know which records, inspection schedules and witness statements tend to establish that.

items.title: Fast action on surveillance video
items.desc: Most Citrus Heights shopping centers and apartment complexes keep footage for a short window before it is erased. A connected attorney can send a preservation demand before the recording is gone.

items.title: Clear guidance on deadlines and shared blame
items.desc: You generally have two years to file, but far less time if a public entity owns the property. Under pure comparative fault, being partly at fault reduces a recovery rather than barring it, and your attorney will explain how that applies to you.

items.question: I fell in a shopping center parking lot on Sunrise Boulevard. Who is actually responsible?
items.answer: It depends on who controlled the area where you fell, which may be the property owner, an individual tenant, a management company or a maintenance contractor. Leases often divide responsibility for sidewalks, lots and interiors differently. An attorney can pull those agreements and identify every party who had a duty to inspect and repair, then determine whether they had notice of the hazard.

items.question: What if I tripped on a public sidewalk in Citrus Heights rather than private property?
items.answer: Claims against a city, Sacramento County or another public agency follow a separate process with a much shorter deadline, measured in months rather than the usual two years. Missing that window can end the claim before it starts. Photograph the defect with something for scale, note the exact location, and reach out for an attorney connection quickly.

items.question: The store says I should have watched where I was walking. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: No. California applies pure comparative fault, so if you are found partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by that percentage rather than eliminated. The owner still has to answer for a hazard they knew or should have known about and failed to fix or mark. Your attorney will gather evidence about lighting, signage and how long the condition existed to address the store's argument.
